holds.reason: This is a 2008 Crescent City harbor and approach survey. Its descriptive report identifies significant channel shoaling, numerous uncharted rocks along the southern offshore edge, and incomplete full-bottom coverage of the approach. The five eligible 4 m screen cells overlapping a predicted-hard polygon (about 80 square meters) cannot establish a natural fishing reef or a safe approach. Keep the survey for harbor-source review; do not promote it to a fishing target without a current chart, site-specific original-cell review and separate substrate evidence.

The 2009 Stil Well Point–Greenwood Cove survey contains fine measured depth and historical rocky-camera overlap, but its original report identifies five dangers to navigation, charted rocks/islets needing correction, and holidays where least depths were not established. The NOAA NBS sample has 60 locally qualified rocky-camera windows, yet only 18 also pass the strict 25 m original-BAG native-grid and depth screen; 37 are held at original fine-grid edges. Do not promote a Fort Bragg–Point Arena target until hazards are reconciled with the current ENC, exact source footprints and position uncertainty are reviewed, and local species/method rules and access pass separately.
